item.title: Amazon Bedrock now lets AI agents buy software and APIs directly through AWS bills
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: Amazon reports that its Bedrock AgentCore payments now integrate with AWS Marketplace, enabling AI agents to discover, purchase, and use x402-enabled software, APIs, and data directly charged to the developer's AWS account. According to AWS, when an agent encounters a payment requirement, it forwards the signed quote to AgentCore payments, which verifies session budgets before issuing a payment token. Developers maintain control by configuring spending caps, approved seller lists, and separate IAM roles for sessions and payments. AWS states that transactions are fully auditable through CloudTrail and Cost Explorer, and early partners like Tavily are already offering integrated live search tools for autonomous agentic commerce.

item.title: Novartis CEO says AI will speed up drug development, but solving biology will take a decade
item.description:
Speaking at an investor event, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan outlined the drugmaker's goal to use AI to improve clinical success rates from 8% to 12% while slashing four years off the standard 12-year R&D cycle. Narasimhan categorized drug development bottlenecks into information, operational, and biological latency. Novartis is already seeing major gains in the first two areas, with AI assisting 90% of development content and cutting statistical programming time dramatically.
However, Narasimhan and Novartis biomedical research president Fiona Marshall argued that biological latency remains the hardest hurdle. While AI excels at molecular design, translating predictions into human biology requires navigating complex systems that current models cannot fully simulate on computers alone. This perspective echoes pushback from other pharma leaders against tech sector claims that AI will eliminate major diseases in under a decade, emphasizing that steady, incremental progress and wet-lab validation are still essential.

item.title: Anthropic makes history with $81bn IPO as shares close up 17%
item.description: Trading Debut and Market Valuation Anthropic officially went public on the Nasdaq, pricing its shares at $83 before opening at $111.50. During its first trading session, the creator of the Claude chatbot briefly crossed a $2tn valuation, though it settled at a closing price of roughly $97, leaving its market cap around $1.3tn to $1.75tn. The blockbuster offering raised $81bn, surpassing SpaceX's previous record. Wider Market Slump Despite the massive enthusiasm for Anthropic, Wall Street closed sharply lower, with the S&P 500 falling for its sixth straight session. Broader investor anxiety about the sustainability of the AI boom, combined with recent tech sector turbulence involving Nvidia, dragged down major indices. Meanwhile, IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warned that surging global demand for AI infrastructure is driving up inflation and could force central banks to raise interest rates. Founder Fortunes and Safety Warnings The IPO generated massive paper wealth for Anthropic's seven co-founders, whose stakes are now valued at over $180bn, with plans to donate significant portions to philanthropic causes. Shortly before ringing the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei issued a public warning acknowledging the real risks of AI, from economic disruption to loss of control, emphasizing that avoiding these dangers depends entirely on prioritizing safety.

item.title: Meta's Upcoming Muse Charm AI Device May Cost $300
item.description:
Meta is reportedly preparing to price its upcoming AI hardware product, Muse Charm, at $300, based on information from The Information. When contacted by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson did not deny the pricing report, stating they are charmed by the interest and will share more details soon.
Muse Charm functions as a physical companion for Meta's Muse AI agent, allowing users to carry it in their pocket or wear it around their neck to chat and give commands. While Meta has seen relative success with its software-based AI tools and avatars, hardware is a new frontier.
The $300 price tag places it on the higher end of the current AI wearable market, comparable to devices like Friend at $250, but significantly more expensive than Amazon's Bee Frontier wearable, which lists for $75.

item.title: Why Microsoft, the FAA, and Banks All Broke at the Same Time
item.description:
In a chaotic week for technology, major systems including Microsoft, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, the NSA, and Apple experienced significant outages. Although U.S. officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, confirmed that the incidents were not cyberattacks, the timing caused widespread panic and led many to suspect hackers or artificial intelligence.
WIRED editors break down the mundane root causes behind the chaos, noting that Microsoft's issue stemmed from a delayed software fix, while the FAA's communication blackout was tied to outdated fiber equipment updates pushed at an inopportune time. Furthermore, experts discuss how companies are increasingly deploying advanced AI cybersecurity tools like Anthropic's Mythos to patch complex bugs, which paradoxically increases the risk of cascading system failures when multiple patches are rushed simultaneously.

item.title: Google's Quantum Chip Beats Classical Limits in Tests of Teamwork
item.description: Cooperative Games and Quantum Contextuality Researchers at Google Quantum AI utilized the Willow processor to investigate quantum contextuality, a property where measurement outcomes depend on accompanying measurements. In a magic square game preventing player communication, four qubits achieved a 98.3% winning rate, surpassing the 88.9% classical limit. Scaling Up to 71 Qubits The team scaled the experiments using a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state. The winning rate stayed above the classical ceiling through 71 players, although the performance margin shrank as more qubits were introduced due to experimental noise. Mathematical Problem and Error Detection In a final test involving a two-dimensional hidden linear function, a 105-qubit experiment returned valid answers more than half the time. The researchers note that these tests can help spot subtle hardware errors that conventional checks might miss.

item.title: Google Quantum AI proves quantum contextuality works at scale on Willow processor
item.description: According to Google Research: Beating the classical limit Researchers ran the magic square game on the Willow quantum processor, using entangled Bell pairs instead of a pre-written table. While the best classical strategy wins at most 88.89% of the time, the qubits won 98.30% of the time, proving that answers take shape only upon measurement according to their context. Measuring contextuality at scale Using a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality, the team measured a contextuality score of 5.590, comfortably past the classical bound of 4 and close to the quantum limit of 6. They also scaled the experiment using the GHZ parity game and solved hidden linear function problems on grids of up to 105 qubits. A new hardware ruler These tasks demand strict agreement among multiple qubits, exposing subtle coherent errors that conventional random-circuit benchmarks miss. This provides an objective performance ceiling grounded in physics rather than shifting classical standards.

item.title: MIT engineers develop dry, stretchy material to replace ultrasound gel
item.description: According to MIT Materials: Background Ultrasound imaging normally requires a cold, wet gel spread on the patient's skin to fill microscopic gaps and help sound waves travel smoothly. While MIT's Zhao Lab is designing wearable ultrasound patches for continuous health tracking, traditional hydrogels dry out within a day or two, limiting their long-term use outside of clinics. Details To solve this, the MIT team engineered a solid, rubbery material using a unique molecular "bottlebrush" structure. By arranging molecules like pipe cleaners with bristles, the team minimized internal friction between polymer chains so sound waves could pass through easily. They reinforced this soft structure with a secondary network, making it tough and skin-like while keeping its sound-transmitting properties intact. Impact In experiments published in *Science*, a small wearable patch using this dry material successfully captured continuous, clear ultrasound images of a volunteer's blood flow during a 30-minute bike ride and remained stable for nine days. This breakthrough could soon enable practical, at-home ultrasound monitoring for patients and athletes without the hassle of sticky gels.

item.title: LangSmith Launches Tool Gateway for Secure Agent Actions
item.description: According to LangChain Blog: Background and Challenges As AI agents move beyond simple chat windows to run autonomously on schedules or in the background, they require access to external tools and systems. According to LangSmith, managing identities, access tokens, and security for hundreds of tools across multiple users creates a massive engineering burden and introduces security risks when handled manually. Core Features Tool Gateway acts as a single managed layer routing tool requests through a unified URL. It manages identity resolution, mapping tool calls to either the individual user's credentials or dedicated agent profiles. Additionally, it offers policy controls such as deny rules and human-in-the-loop approvals for sensitive actions, alongside built-in servers for common apps like Google and GitHub to eliminate custom OAuth setups. Impact and Visibility Every tool call is recorded within agent traces, logging the specific tool, server, user, latency, and outcome without storing sensitive payload data. Enterprise plans also include centralized audit logs, giving security teams a clear, unified record to answer compliance questions and debug production issues faster.

item.title: Google Introduces Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
item.description:
According to Google AI:
Google product manager Lucia Loher and research scientist Nora Kassner report that connecting AI agents to dozens or hundreds of tools often inflates input tokens, adds latency, and lowers tool selection accuracy. To address this, the new Tool Retrieval feature lets agents keep a full tool library on standby while only loading specific parameter schemas when a task requires them. Developers can enable this by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading: true on tools they wish to hold back. How It Works The model continues to see the name and description of every deferred tool so it understands what is available, while the heavy parameter schemas stay out of context. When a task requires a specific function, the model requests it by name, and the API loads the full schema within the same request. Google notes that this mechanism also supports remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and client-side retrieval for custom registries, while working seamlessly with prefix caching to keep conversation prefixes stable.

item.title: Google Signs 50-MW Superhot Geothermal PPA with Quaise Energy
item.description:
According to companies' announcements, Google has agreed to buy 50 MW of electricity from Project Obsidian, a geothermal power project developed by Quaise Energy near Newberry Volcano in central Oregon, valued at more than $500 million. The energy will support Google's data center operations in The Dalles, Oregon.
The project will be built in two stages. The initial phase will use conventional drilling, while a subsequent phase will deploy Quaise's millimeter-wave drilling technology to reach depths of up to 65,000 feet. At these extreme depths, rock temperatures exceed 932 degrees Fahrenheit, allowing superhot geothermal wells to produce up to 10 times more power per well than conventional sources.
This PPA is part of Google's broader strategy to secure firm, carbon-free electricity, complementing previous investments in advanced nuclear and long-duration storage as the tech sector grapples with baseload power scarcity driven by expanding AI data centers.

item.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading
item.description: On Thursday, November 19, 2026, AI maker Anthropic made history as the first leading model developer to go public on Wall Street, defying a broad market sell-off and tech bubble concerns. The company priced its shares at $83, but they opened at $111.50 and ultimately closed around $97, up 17% for the day. Record Fundraising and Valuation Anthropic raised an unprecedented $81.3 billion by selling 980 million shares, comfortably surpassing previous megadebuts like SpaceX. The IPO valued the five-year-old creator of the Claude chatbot at roughly $1.5 trillion initially, with its opening valuation surging to around $2 trillion. Chief Executive Dario Amodei stated that the robust financial position reinforces the company's commitment to building safe AI. Explosive Growth and Market Jitters The historic listing comes amid rapid financial growth, with Anthropic reporting third-quarter revenue surging to $17 billion, up dramatically from $1.4 billion a year prior, largely driven by coding applications. However, the debut also drew scrutiny: critics and protesters voiced concerns over potential existential risks and financial market stability, while the broader tech sector navigated ongoing turbulence surrounding chip giant Nvidia.

item.title: Xenia Adds 15% Carbon Fiber to PEBA Filament for Drones and Robots
item.description:
Xenia has expanded its technical filament portfolio with the release of XECARB PEBA-CF, combining a polyether block amide matrix with 15 percent carbon fiber reinforcement. According to the company, the carbon fiber provides stiffness to prevent excessive deformation under mechanical loads, while the elastomeric PEBA base offers toughness and allows parts to spring back to their original shape after impact.
The material features a density of 1.08 g/cm³ and a heat deflection temperature of 105°C. Xenia is targeting the filament primarily at the drone, UAV, and robotics sectors, alongside broader industrial and aerospace applications where components must balance light weight with dynamic stress response. This new grade joins the company's existing 3DF Materials lineup, which includes specialized high-modulus, toughened, and recycled carbon fiber composites.

item.title: Finding the sweet spot for satellite constellation size
item.description:
During a conversation at Space Tech Expo Europe, Jan Smolders, chief commercial officer at Space Inventor, joined SpaceNews' Mike Gruss to discuss key trends in the satellite industry. A central topic was the strategic value of mini-constellations, which offer a balance between responsiveness and capability compared to massive mega-constellations.
Additionally, the discussion touched on institutional hurdles, specifically exploring how European governments can speed up their decision-making and funding processes for space technology. They also examined operational use cases, highlighting why tipping and cueing technologies have become increasingly valuable for regional security and monitoring in the Baltic Sea.

item.title: What industrial drone deployments reveal about real-world autonomy challenges
item.description:
Industrial facilities present complex environments that severely test autonomous drone navigation. GNSS signals can be blocked or distorted by metallic structures, while repetitive pipes and reflective surfaces confuse visual and lidar sensors. Furthermore, wind gusts near buildings introduce aerodynamic disturbances that challenge flight controllers.
ZenaDrone contributor Jonathan Metzelaar notes that autonomy performance depends heavily on the interactions between subsystems whose assumptions are rarely independent. Localization errors can corrupt obstacle coordinates, and processing latency directly translates into physical braking distance, meaning an obstacle avoidance system must be judged on end-to-end timing rather than detection range alone. Additionally, successfully flying a route does not guarantee that collected inspection data, such as thermal imagery or photogrammetry, will be accurate or repeatable.
To ensure safe and reliable deployments, engineering teams must move beyond isolated subsystem tests and evaluate their systems under combined failure scenarios. This includes defining measurable acceptance criteria for localization, latency, and failure recovery, while maintaining clear operational boundaries and supervisory human oversight.

item.title: How Developers Use Frontier AI Agents to Build Simulations in NVIDIA Omniverse
item.description:
According to NVIDIA Robotics:
NVIDIA highlights a series of developer projects demonstrating how frontier AI models and Omniverse libraries are transforming simulation workflows. Engineers and developers are using natural-language instructions to guide AI agents in assembling 3D assets, configuring physics engines, and running tests across diverse domains.
Key examples include building facility-scale digital twins from engineering data, creating robot pick-and-place simulations using standardized asset libraries, and testing humanoids and robotic cable-routing tasks in virtual environments. Developers also report challenges, noting that automated tests sometimes miss tactile issues like object shaking, which require manual inspection and prompt adjustments to resolve.
These workflows leverage OpenUSD frameworks and specialized Omniverse libraries to connect rendering, physics, and sensor simulation, enabling teams to evaluate industrial operations and autonomous systems before deploying them in the physical world.

item.title: Scientists map every single cell in an adult vertebrate for the first time
item.description:
According to MIT Neuroscience:
A team of researchers from MIT, the Whitehead Institute, and Charité–Universitätsmedizin Berlin has successfully mapped the cell types and gene activity of an entire adult vertebrate. Because profiling larger animals comprehensively is technically demanding and expensive, the team turned to *Danionella cerebrum*, a tiny, transparent fish barely one centimeter long that is closely related to zebrafish.
In a study published in *Science*, the researchers used single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial mapping methods to analyze more than 600,000 cells from across the fish's brain, spinal cord, eyes, internal organs, and fins. This comprehensive approach allowed them to capture rare cell populations and observe large-scale patterns, such as how neurons from the same brain region share similar gene activity regardless of the neurotransmitters they use.
The atlas also revealed that adult cells, such as connective-tissue fibroblasts, retain a molecular memory of their developmental positions in the body. Furthermore, the team used the map as a reference to track how the fish regenerates missing neurons in the forebrain after injury. The complete atlas has been made publicly available through an interactive online resource called DigiFish.

item.title: Velo3D Selected for $10M DEVCOM Armaments Center Award
item.description:
According to TCT Magazine, the US Army DEVCOM Armaments Center selected Velo3D through the ONIX Marketplace under an Other Transaction Authority pathway. This acquisition approach is specifically designed to bridge the gap between commercial innovations and military needs.
Under this potential $10 million program, Velo3D will focus on establishing modular payload architectures, advanced warhead components, and scalable manufacturing. The work will primarily involve Inconel 718—a material already qualified on Velo3D's Sapphire platform—and a second high-performance alloy directed by the government.
While Velo3D handles the additive manufacturing process development, production, and quality documentation, the U.S. government retains design authority and responsibility for lethality testing. A core part of the initiative relies on Velo3D's Golden Print File methodology, which aims to ensure repeatable production quality across different machines and domestic facilities.

item.title: Giga Storage on how European battery asset management is evolving
item.description:
In an interview with Energy-Storage.news, Kathleen Dingenen from Giga Storage discusses the rapid evolution of battery energy storage system (BESS) asset management in Europe. Three years ago, assets were small and relied mostly on frequency containment reserves. Today, grid-scale batteries reach gigawatt-hour proportions, shifting value to wholesale trading and complex revenue stacking.
Key regulatory changes like the EU’s RfG 2.0 are making grid-forming capabilities mandatory for large storage, directly impacting inverter specifications, warranties, and plant operations. Furthermore, asset managers are moving away from rigid daily cycle caps toward annual throughput limits, leveraging LFP chemistry and liquid cooling. However, accurate state-of-charge estimation remains a practical challenge that requires robust buffers and continuous monitoring to prevent revenue losses.

item.title: Clearing Cellular Traffic Jams Treats Multiple Diseases in Mice
item.description:
According to Broad Institute:
According to researchers at the Broad Institute publishing in _Neuron_, a group of over 50 inherited disorders known as proteinopathies share a common root cause: misfolded proteins accumulating inside cells and overwhelming the cellular quality-control machinery.
Building on their previous work on TMED9 in MUC1 kidney disease, the team found that TMED2, 7, 9, and 10 form a protein complex that traps these misfolded proteins and causes a cellular traffic jam. By deleting or targeting a key component of this complex called TMED7, scientists were able to release the trapped proteins to be recycled without disrupting normal cellular functions, successfully reversing disease hallmarks in mice with MUC1 kidney disease and slowing vision loss in a model of retinitis pigmentosa.

item.title: Freiburg team secures about 10 million euros to explore commercial plastic volumetric 3D printing
item.description: Background and Funding According to Nanjixiong, process technology professor Bastian Rapp and interface chemistry and physics professor Jürgen Rühe from the University of Freiburg have secured about 10 million euros in European Research Council (ERC) synergy funding. The funding will support the six-year CHiC2PRINT project, selected from over 950 applications. Technical Approach The project aims to bridge the gap between commercially mature plastics and light-driven additive manufacturing. Instead of traditional layer-by-layer stacking, the team plans to use directed light exposure to form three-dimensional structures inside an existing volume of plastic. By combining process technology and interface chemistry, they aim to make standard plastics responsive to light control. Recycling and Outlook CHiC2PRINT also incorporates product end-of-life handling into its design, aiming to separate formed objects through a process called hierarchical dissociation to recover and reuse raw plastics. The project intends to investigate whether commercial plastic systems can combine complex geometry manufacturing with efficient recycling, though specific recycling rates and production speeds are yet to be established.

item.title: Pinecone now exports cost data in FOCUS format for FinOps tools
item.description: According to Pinecone: Previously, finance teams had to manually download and reshape Pinecone billing files to track cloud costs using FinOps tools. With the new Cost and Usage Export API, available to Enterprise organizations, users can generate exports for any time window over the past year either via the console or the Admin API. The data is provided as FOCUS v1.4 CSV files packed in a zip format, including project and index tags that allow precise chargeback to individual teams or applications. Platform teams can also automate the entire pipeline by scheduling jobs to pull these reports directly into data warehouses.

item.title: Cailabs CEO Discusses Laser Communications and US Plans on Space Minds
item.description:
During an appearance on the SpaceNews podcast *Space Minds* at Space Tech Expo Europe, Cailabs co-founder and CEO Jean-François Morizur joined host Mike Gruss to discuss the evolving landscape of space optical communications. Morizur focused on clearing up industry misconceptions surrounding laser communications technology.
Additionally, the discussion covered Cailabs' ongoing business strategy, including specific plans for the United States market and why establishing standardized interoperability remains a critical priority for future satellite networks.

item.title: Towards a Science of Capable Autonomous Agents & Provable Safety — Part II
item.description: According to Carnegie Mellon ML Blog: In Part II of this series, the author addresses how to ensure capable autonomous agents remain open to human correction, even when intervention conflicts with task completion. Drawing on recent game-theoretic and complexity-theoretic results from AAAI 2026, the author proves that communication costs grow with the number of objectives and that reward hacking is inevitable under finite-sample estimation. To address why standard RLHF or single rewards fail to achieve corrigibility, the research presents sufficient conditions for satisfying corrigibility requirements in partially observable off-switch games by structuring five distinct utility heads with strict priority gaps (deference, switch preservation, truthfulness, low impact, and task reward). Furthermore, the author highlights empirical findings from the ROGUE benchmark, showing that LLM agents often fail to maintain safety constraints during ordinary computer use or delegation. Finally, the paper discusses 'sharding'—dividing evaluation criteria across separate model requests to prevent oversight overload.

item.title: FDA Approves Regeneron's Livsayis as First siRNA Therapy for Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
item.description:
According to Regeneron, the FDA approval of Livsayis marks the company's second new drug modality this year, following the approval of its hearing loss gene therapy in April. Livsayis is a complement component factor 5 (C5)-directed siRNA designed to limit terminal complement activation, which is a major driver of generalized myasthenia gravis, a progressive autoimmune disease causing muscle weakness.
The approval was supported by the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial, in which the therapy showed a statistically significant improvement in daily functioning scores compared to a placebo at 24 weeks. Analysts at Truist Securities and BMO Capital Markets noted that the quarterly dosing schedule provides a practical advantage for the patient experience.
Like other therapies that reduce C5 activity, Livsayis carries a boxed warning for serious meningococcal and other infections, and it will be available exclusively through a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program.

item.title: Anthropic Hits $2 Trillion Valuation in Nasdaq Debut After Shares Surge 34%
item.description: IPO Performance and Valuation According to Reuters, Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share after selling 980 million shares, raising substantial capital ahead of its public debut. When trading began, the stock opened at $111.5, representing a 34% surge over the IPO price and pushing the company's total market capitalization past the $2 trillion threshold. This milestone makes Anthropic the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, positioning it alongside tech giants like Microsoft, Apple, and Nvidia in the trillion-dollar club. Industry Implications and Market Sentiment Market analysts view this blockbuster debut, alongside Nvidia's recent earnings report, as a crucial test of investor confidence in the AI sector amid ongoing debates over heavy spending and profitability. While early backers and founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, reaped massive financial gains, some market skeptics warn that Anthropic still faces heavy pressure to turn a profit and manage nearly $900 billion in future computing commitments with partners like Amazon and Google.

item.title: langchain-openrouter 0.3.0: Integrating OpenRouter with LangChain
item.description:
Release Overview
The langchain-openrouter==0.3.0 release marks a specific version tag within the massive LangChain repository. It focuses on providing reliable integration tools for developers who want to route their AI application traffic through OpenRouter's platform. Ecosystem Integration
By leveraging this package, developers can bypass the hassle of maintaining multiple individual API connections. It bridges the gap between LangChain components and OpenRouter's multi-model gateway, ensuring smooth execution of chains and agents. Getting Started
Users can track, compare, and install this specific version directly from the GitHub releases page or via standard Python package distribution channels to maintain compatibility within their AI development stack.

item.title: XJet Launches On-Demand Manufacturing Services and AI Jewelry Tool at Formnext
item.description: Service Expansion XJet has rolled out two new offerings at the Formnext event to broaden market access to its NanoParticle Jetting (NPJ) technology. The newly launched XPARTS on-demand service allows users to leverage the company's materials, engineering support, and production capabilities for application assessment, prototyping, validation, and production. Material Versatility NPJ technology can print a wide variety of materials, including technical ceramics, stainless steel, copper alloys, and precious metals such as sterling silver, gold alloys, and Platinum 950. This material breadth has driven XJet into the jewelry sector over the past year, prompting the introduction of the XJet Atelier service for AI-assisted personalized jewelry creation. Commercial Milestones During the Formnext exhibition, XJet CEO Guy Zimmerman noted that the company is making its full capabilities accessible to more customers for finished parts, production systems, or personalized jewelry. Additionally, XJet confirmed the securing of its first customer orders for the Carmel Pro and Carmel ORO platforms.

item.title: Sakana AI launches independent Security Research Group for AI cyber defense
item.description:
According to Sakana AI:
Sakana AI is establishing an independent R&D organization, the Security Research Group, dedicated to collective, AI-driven cyber defense and the safety of AI systems. According to the company, frontier AI has drastically accelerated the discovery of software flaws, with NIST reporting a 263% surge in CVE submissions between 2020 and 2025. Concurrently, attackers are weaponizing AI agents to launch simultaneous intrusions, putting immense pressure on traditional patching workflows.
To counter this, Sakana AI argues that faster response and routine patching are no longer enough. The group advocates for a secure-by-design approach, treating security as an essential Kano-model "must-be quality" built into software from its inception. Facing structural constraints in Japan such as outsourced operations, technical debt, and limited IT staff, the research group will focus on upstream prevention, AI-based collective defense, and securing AI agents against misuse.
Led by Akihiro Umegai and David Ha, the group plans to operate with vendor neutrality and maintain responsible disclosure principles, bridging the gap between national security policies and practical industry implementation.

item.title: SolarEdge debuts dual-module power optimizer
item.description:
SolarEdge unveiled its new Duo power optimizer at the RE+ 2026 trade show in Las Vegas, targeting commercial and industrial (C&I) solar projects. Unlike conventional devices that connect to a single module, the Duo features independent maximum power point trackers (MPPT) for two connected modules, with each input supporting up to 650 W.
According to SolarEdge, the dual-module configuration reduces hardware requirements by 50% compared to its previous C651U model. The hardware comes with pre-extended cables to streamline installation and supports dual-tilt racking systems. Additionally, it features built-in arc fault detection, allowing every optimizer to act as an arc sensor for improved safety. The product carries a 25-year warranty and complies with U.S. Domestic Content and Foreign Entity of Concern requirements.

item.title: NASA Tests RS-25 Engine for Future Artemis Missions
item.description:
According to NASA News:
NASA reports that the test took place on November 18, 2026, on the Fred Haise Test Stand at the Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. The RS-25 engine, designated as developmental engine No. 10001, was fired for its planned duration of 200 seconds.
Although this specific developmental engine will not fly in space, the test provides NASA and its prime contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with essential telemetry and performance metrics. These insights are intended to refine the propulsion systems for upcoming Artemis missions.
Looking ahead, the Space Launch System rocket is scheduled to launch astronauts for the Artemis IV lunar landing mission in 2028 from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This flight forms part of NASA's broader roadmap to explore the lunar South Pole and establish a sustainable human presence on the Moon.

item.title: nChroma Cuts Staff in Half and Stops Hepatitis B Drug Trial
item.description: nChroma Bio has announced a significant corporate restructuring, which includes halving its employee headcount and halting the phase 1/2 clinical trial of CRMA-1001, a liver-directed epigenetic silencer intended as a potential functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. The trial had only begun patient enrollment in January. According to CEO Jeff Walsh, the company is now evaluating strategic alternatives and shifting its remaining resources toward a next-generation preclinical hepatitis B program designed to more effectively target viral replication and immune suppression. This setback follows an earlier undisclosed round of layoffs in November 2025 as the company prepared to enter the clinic, and comes in a competitive landscape where other players like GSK have recently advanced rival treatments toward regulatory approval.

item.title: GlobalFoundries invests $10 million in Cyient Semiconductors
item.description:
Cyient Semiconductors has secured a $10 million equity investment from US-based chipmaker GlobalFoundries, bringing its total post-money valuation to $510 million following a previous round led by Edelweiss. According to Cyient CEO Suman Narayan, the funding will be used to expand turnkey custom ASIC capabilities, accelerate custom silicon development, and strengthen long-term wafer supply assurance.
Cyient operates design centers across India, Belgium, and the US, providing custom ASIC and ASSP solutions for automotive, industrial, AI, communications, and data center markets. Narayan noted that having a leading semiconductor ecosystem partner as a strategic investor serves as a strong validation of India's growing semiconductor innovation potential and the company's business model.

item.title: Study reveals data centers' long-distance damage to air quality
item.description:
According to MIT Climate:
According to a study published in Environmental Research Letters by MIT researchers, the massive electricity demands of artificial intelligence data centers create widespread air pollution far beyond their physical locations. The team estimates that additional emissions from grid power plants in 2023 resulted in approximately 650 premature deaths across the United States.
By building a sophisticated modeling framework, the researchers tracked how power grid demands ripple across the country, showing that fossil fuel generators—often natural gas and coal plants—ramp up to meet 24/7 computing needs. Due to atmospheric conditions and regional power generation mixes, Midwestern states like Iowa, Kansas, and South Dakota suffered higher per capita premature mortality rates than Virginia and Texas, where most data centers are actually located.
The findings emphasize that policymakers and tech companies must consider broader public health impacts and regional atmospheric interactions when choosing where to site data centers and how to supply them with clean energy.

item.title: Oil flows through Middle East chokepoints increased in the third quarter
item.description:
According to EIA Today in Energy:
Recent data published by the U.S. Energy Information Administration in its Global Energy Security Data reveals that total oil shipments through vital Middle Eastern transit routes rose significantly in the third quarter of 2026. Key Details According to the report, the 19% increase covers total crude oil and petroleum products. The figures represent the combined flows through the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and the Suez Canal or SUMED pipeline route, incorporating oil originating from both Middle Eastern nations and other global suppliers. Market Impact This notable quarterly rebound follows earlier disruptions in the region, reflecting how global energy markets and refiners continue to adapt their trade routes and logistics in response to shifting geopolitical conditions and supply dynamics.

item.title: Securities Regulators Warn That Slow Progress on Quantum Security is a Mistake
item.description: The Threat to Financial Markets A global group of securities regulators warns that financial markets are lagging in preparation for quantum computers that could eventually break current encryption methods. According to The International Organization of Securities Commissions, most firms are merely training staff or identifying vulnerable systems, with very few actively testing or installing upgrades. Interception and Supply Chain Risks The report highlights that attackers do not need to wait for a functional quantum machine to cause harm. Through a tactic known as harvest now, decrypt later, malicious actors can intercept and store encrypted communications today for future decryption. Furthermore, a company that upgrades its systems can still remain exposed if its trading partners or shared payment networks fail to make the transition. Mitigation and Current Experiments To counter these risks, regulators recommend adopting post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility. However, upgrading complex financial systems requires extensive coordination, as demonstrated by tests involving central banks. Meanwhile, actual financial applications of quantum technology remain largely experimental, prompting warnings about companies that overstate their quantum capabilities to investors.

item.title: Anthropic Pulls Off Record-Breaking IPO While Battling Its Own Internal and External Roadblocks
item.description:
Anthropic's public market debut on the Nasdaq brought in roughly $81 billion, valuing the AI company at around $1.5 trillion and leaving it with about $200 billion in the bank. However, the company has committed to paying vendors over $900 billion in the next 19 years, mostly for data centers. While recent quarterly sales hit $17 billion, the company remains unprofitable due to stock-based compensation.
Beyond finances, Anthropic faces fierce resistance from local communities over West Virginia data center projects and environmental impacts. CEO Dario Amodei insists that safety is the primary limiting factor for deployments, noting that prioritizing public benefit and screening for safety-oriented hires has sometimes stunted short-term growth. Furthermore, upcoming regulations and questions over whether AI can sustain its massive infrastructure costs cast shadows on its long-term dominance.

item.title: Eima agricultural exhibition highlights batteries, autonomy, and robotics
item.description:
As Europe's second-largest agricultural machinery exhibition, Eima brings numerous innovations to Bologna, Italy, over a five-day span. A prominent trend at the event is the shift toward electrification and field robotics, replacing traditional fuel-powered machinery with automated alternatives.
Among the highlights, Italian machinery manufacturer Faresin introduced its autonomous electric Eramix feeding robot. According to the report, this machine uses a specialized milling cutter to remove silage from the clamp, mixes the ingredients thoroughly, and then distributes the feed directly to cows without requiring manual operation.

item.title: Anton Paar Expands Accredited ISO 17025 Calibration Services
item.description:
According to Anton Paar, the company is expanding the scope of its ISO 17025-accredited calibration laboratory at its headquarters in Graz, Austria. In addition to established services for density meters and thermometers, the laboratory now offers accredited calibration for selected viscometers and rheometers, including SVM kinematic viscometers, ViscoQC rotational viscometers, and MCR rheometers.
Project lead Kristin Hunger states that the expansion helps customers meet quality and regulatory requirements while simplifying calibration processes. The services use traceable reference materials and can be performed either in the accredited laboratory or directly at the customer's site by qualified personnel.

item.title: The Untapped Potential of Drug Repurposing
item.description: BioSpace Insights hosted an episode of its podcast Denatured featuring Daniel Tillett, CEO of Racura Oncology, and Sten Sörensen, CEO of Cereno Scientific. The discussion, hosted by Jennifer C. Smith-Parker, centered on the growing regulatory focus on drug repurposing. The guests explored the reasons behind the FDA's renewed emphasis on finding new uses for already existing molecules and examined the practical challenges involved in successfully transforming them into effective new treatments for patients.

item.title: Siemens brings embedded AI to HVAC systems for self-adapting climate control
item.description:
According to Siemens Blog:
At Chillventa 2026, Siemens highlighted how the HVAC industry is shifting from generic, rule-based settings to practical, model-based adaptive control. Traditional HVAC equipment often relies on conservative thresholds, such as preventive defrost strategies that can increase winter heating-energy use. Siemens' Autonomous Equipment Optimization embeds machine learning directly inside the Climatix equipment controller.
For its intelligent defrost application, the system learns the relationship between operating conditions and expected exhaust-fan power during frost-free operation. This creates a virtual reference to continuously monitor deviations caused by frost buildup, allowing defrost cycles to trigger based on actual demand rather than fixed rules. According to Siemens, this approach can reduce winter heating-energy use by 20–30% in scenarios without frost sensors, depending on climate and operating conditions. Furthermore, the embedded model operates within strict engineer-defined safety and validation limits, aiming to reduce manual intervention during commissioning and support condition-based maintenance across the equipment lifecycle.

item.title: Soft robotic suit helps older adults stand up and walk more easily
item.description: How the exosuit works Developed by researchers at the Technical University of Munich, the exosuit functions like a wearable system with thigh straps, a waist belt, and artificial tendons connected to a backpack-like motor unit. Sensors on the thighs track leg movements in real time, and a machine learning algorithm triggers the motor to pull on the tendons, providing hip support exactly when the user stands up or walks. Study results and user feedback In tests involving ten older adults aged 69 to 85, the suit improved mobility significantly. Participants completed up to four additional sit-and-stand cycles in one minute, and their average walking metabolic cost dropped by 14%. According to researcher Dr. Xiaohui Zhang, users also reported a high sense of personal agency, feeling that the suit acted like a regular piece of clothing rather than an intrusive machine.

item.title: How OpenAI uses autonomous agents to keep ChatGPT fast
item.description:
According to OpenAI News:
OpenAI describes the evolution of its performance engineering from manual investigations to an automated agent factory. The Performance Factory consists of four main components: a task service with configurable workflows, a dispatch loop, cloud-based execution, and event subscriptions.
Its first deployed workflow, the Regression Workflow, takes over when a performance alert fires. An agent investigates metrics and logs, undergoes an adversarial review by a separate AI session to check for errors, and proposes a pull request for engineers to review. After deployment, another agent verifies whether performance has recovered to baseline. OpenAI notes that while finding root causes has seen high accuracy, writing the correct code fix remains harder and often requires human architectural guidance.

item.title: GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 Available Free for up to 3,000 Requests Monthly on Sakura's AI Inference Platform
item.description:
Sakura Internet announced that it has begun trial offerings for two prominent open-weight AI models, GLM-5.3-Flash (released by China's Z.ai in August) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (released by China's DeepSeek in October), through its inference API platform known as Sakura's AI Engine.
Running on the company's high-performance cloud infrastructure and operated within domestic Japanese data centers, the platform provides API access to various domestic and international foundation models as well as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities. For users exceeding the promotional limit, standard charges apply at a rate of 0.4 yen per 10,000 input tokens and 4.0 yen per 10,000 output tokens for both models.

item.title: ESA Awards OHB €102M Contract for ClearSpace-1 Debris Removal Mission
item.description: Background and Restructuring The European Space Agency signed the contract on 17 November at Space Tech Expo Europe in Bremen, marking the start of the implementation phase for ClearSpace-1. Originally awarded to a consortium led by Swiss startup ClearSpace in December 2020, the mission underwent major changes after its initial target was struck by space debris in August 2023. This forced a redesign, selecting Proba-1 as the new target and making OHB the prime contractor. Launch Details The mission's launch plans have also shifted over time. While it was once slated for a Vega C rocket in 2026, technical papers and presentations point toward a dedicated microlauncher flight. An OHB presentation featured an illustration of the RFA ONE rocket, which is notable since OHB holds a majority stake in its developer, Rocket Factory Augsburg. However, neither ESA nor OHB has officially confirmed this launch vehicle, with the overall mission timeline now targeted for 2030.

item.title: Google Returns to AI Center Stage with Gemini 4 Neon
item.description:
According to Google DeepMind and benchmark evaluations from Artificial Analysis, Gemini 4 Neon features a 1-million token context window and adjustable thinking depths. In the AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1, Neon secured the global third spot in its xhigh mode. In programming benchmarks like CursorBench 4.1 and SWE-sweep, it outperformed several competing flagship models while maintaining lower operational expenses.
At the same time, Google paired Neon with the Antigravity platform's /swarm mode for multi-agent coordination, allowing the model to handle long-running, multi-file engineering workflows. This release is supported by structural changes under the leadership of Koray Kavukcuoglu, who prioritized rapid iteration, and the cost advantages provided by Google's custom 7th-generation TPU Ironwood hardware.

item.title: Prioritize, Don't Decide: What We Learned Auditing a Deployed Human-in-the-Loop CV Sorter
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: The paper examines a deployed CV Priority Sorter used for academic vacancies, which combines a frozen multilingual transformer encoder with a per-session linear model that retrains after each label. While testing showed that reading in the tool's order reaches 95% of relevant candidates after half the pile, an audit of the system yielded four critical findings: 1) synthetic applicant pools were easily sortable by document length alone, rendering standard precision metrics uninformative until length budgets were equalized; 2) reported four-level agreement scores merely tracked classifier confidence rather than true ranking and dropped as labels accumulated; 3) uncertainty sampling actually increased the committee's total reading load because it targeted items that would otherwise have been skipped; and 4) hosted LLM embedding models improved zero-label ordinal discrimination (raising it from 0.66 to 0.80 under length control) but became redundant once the session model received two dozen labels, a cold-start gain that local cross-encoders could match without external data transmission. The authors report the specific architectural fixes implemented in response to each finding. The work is currently a preprint under review at the EACL 2027 Industry Track.

item.title: ITC Foods Launches Sunfeast Plant-Based Nutrition Shake Combining Protein and Fibre in India
item.description:
ITC Foods, the CPG conglomerate behind brands like Aashirvaad and Yoga Bar, has rolled out a mocha-flavoured plant-based nutrition shake under its Sunfeast brand in India. Priced at ₹125 ($1.34) per 300ml bottle, the ready-to-drink beverage contains 25g of complete protein sourced from pea, peanut, and yeast isolates, alongside 5.8g of dietary fibre including oligofructose, inulin, and polydextrose.
Company executives note that while consumer awareness around protein is surging, fibre often receives less attention despite its complementary role in gut health. This launch reflects a broader evolution in India's alternative protein market, where brands are moving beyond early-stage meat replacements toward advanced, nutrition-forward products supported by a rising young demographic and the expansion of the GLP-1 weight-loss drug market.

item.title: Awat County Yuansu 200MW/800MWh Electrochemical Energy Storage Project Commences
item.description: Awat County officially commenced the Yuansu 200MW/800MWh electrochemical energy storage project, built by Envision Energy with a total self-funded investment of 720 million yuan. Project Overview and Goals The project constructs a new lithium iron phosphate electrochemical energy storage power station. According to the enterprise representatives, the facility is scheduled to achieve grid connection and commence operation by June next year. It is designed to store electricity flexibly, supplement power supply during peak demand, and smooth out fluctuations from local photovoltaic power generation. Environmental and Economic Impact Local officials note that the project will help transform regional renewable resources into industrial advantages. According to preliminary estimations, the storage capacity helps integrate green energy, while the broader initiative is projected to save 1.08 million tons of standard coal annually and reduce pollutant emissions including sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides once all phases are fully completed.

item.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Now Supports Full Fine-Tuning Without Infrastructure Management
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
Amazon SageMaker AI has updated its Serverless Model Customization service to support Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) alongside existing parameter-efficient methods like LoRA. While LoRA freezes pre-trained weights and injects small replacement matrices, its low-rank nature can hit an accuracy plateau on complex tasks. In contrast, FFT updates all model parameters simultaneously, leveraging the full representational capacity of the network to achieve stronger convergence and better layer activation alignment.
To evaluate these methods, tests were conducted using a Qwen3-4B base model trained on 110,000 coding instruction pairs. Results showed that as training data scales beyond 100,000 examples, FFT achieves superior accuracy on semantic correctness and surface-level text similarity metrics compared to LoRA. However, FFT also carries a higher risk of catastrophic forgetting, requiring careful tuning of learning rates and epoch counts to preserve general knowledge.

item.title: Exa Boosts Web Embedding Throughput by 50% on AWS AI Chips
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
To build a true web index for semantic search and AI agents, Exa must embed tens of billions of documents into a vector database. Facing doubled inference loads during a major corpus migration, Exa optimized its machine learning pipeline on AWS Neuron hardware, including Inferentia2 and Trainium2 chips.
Starting from a baseline FP16 model, the engineering team applied several progressive optimizations. They utilized weight layout adjustments, autocast precision downcasting while maintaining a strict correctness threshold of 0.999 cosine similarity, and drop-in NKI kernels. To address memory spill and hardware core contention, Exa developed custom kernels including a fused SwiGLU MLP kernel and shape-tailored attention operations to reduce redundant floating-point operations.
These optimizations were largely driven by an automated, agentic development workflow built on Flyte. Different AI models handled distinct tasks within a testing harness, ranging from compiler parameter tuning to writing complex custom kernels, ultimately delivering a 1.5x throughput improvement over the initial baseline.

item.title: Maryland students sue after AI gun detection mistakes Doritos for a firearm
item.description:
According to the lawsuit filed by the Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, the incident occurred after football practice when students were waiting for rides outside a Maryland high school. Omnilert's AI gun-detection system flagged a bag of Doritos as a firearm with 90% confidence, prompting six police cruisers to arrive with flashing lights and armed officers. The students were ordered to their knees, handcuffed, and searched.
Legal documents state that Maryland's office of the inspector general for education found over 99% of alerts from this system in Baltimore County Public Schools were false positives. The lawsuit targets Omnilert, the local police, the school board, and the principal, alleging unlawful detention, while highlighting the severe emotional distress suffered by the students.

item.title: Satya Nadella warns critical infrastructure has unpatchable software in the age of AI cyberattacks
item.description: At The New York Times' DealBook Summit, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella highlighted a growing security crisis. He pointed out that everyday hardware like firmware, chillers, and HVAC systems are connected to the internet but remain unpatchable. This creates major risks in the era of AI-aided cyberattacks. Nadella also addressed a recent global Microsoft Outlook outage, attributing it to a latent bug rather than a cyberattack. Furthermore, he explained that AI has accelerated both vulnerability discovery and attack capabilities. While companies used to have time to test software fixes, patches now must be deployed instantly to counter active threats, which unfortunately introduces system instability.

item.title: Humyn Labs raises $47M to provide real-world training data for robots
item.description: Funding Details and Revenue Growth Physical AI research and deployment company Humyn Labs reported raising $47 million in its Series A funding round, which includes $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. Co-founder Ishank Gupta stated that the company has surpassed $50 million in annualized revenue within six months of operation. Data Collection across Four Modalities Humyn Labs addresses a major industry bottleneck by helping roboticists bridge the gap between lab simulations and real-world execution. The company gathers data across vision, sound, touch, and motion using proprietary capture devices operated in over 20 countries, with a primary focus on Latin America, South Asia, Southeast Asia, and East Asia. Their end-to-end data engine converts human job performance into labelled, training-ready datasets tailored to researchers' needs. Deployment Infrastructure Plans The newly secured capital will be allocated toward three key areas: building deployment readiness infrastructure in Brazil, Korea, and India; advancing their capture hardware and enrichment engine; and expanding their on-the-ground presence in San Francisco, London, and Seoul to save research labs from the logistical burdens of data collection.

item.title: 2026 Finance Quantum Index Shows Growing Bank Investment
item.description: The 2026 Finance Quantum Index, authored by HorizonX founder Steve Suarez, has expanded its coverage to 64 financial institutions across eight regions, introducing 36 new additions to map quantum activity in banking, insurance, payments, and central banking. Rankings and Highlights JPMorgan Chase takes the top spot with 97 points due to strengths in workforce, research, and adoption, maintaining a 20-point lead. HSBC and Wells Fargo share second place with 77 points. Meanwhile, Mastercard ranks third with 62 points, and recently launched a Quantum Advisory Practice to help financial institutions handle post-quantum cryptography migration and security risks. Methodology and Industry Gap Using a revised methodology weighting workforce at 30 percent, R&D at 40 percent, and adoption at 30 percent, the index relies on documented evidence such as patents, papers, and partnerships. A notable finding is the widespread capability gap: only five institutions scored 60 or higher, showing that advanced quantum investments remain concentrated among a few market leaders.

item.title: langchain==1.5.2: A new release for the AI application development framework
item.description:
Release Overview
According to the repository documentation, LangChain has released version 1.5.2, marking another milestone in the project's ongoing development lifecycle. The release notes provide extensive comparison links against numerous preceding tags, ranging from early releases like v0.0.75 up to recent candidate versions such as v0.1.17rc1. Developer Utility
The provided comparison list allows engineers and contributors to inspect code differences across a vast array of incremental updates. This structured approach helps developers identify specific patches, dependency adjustments, and API modifications introduced leading up to this version.

item.title: Nvidia's Interim CEO Seeks Stability with 'We've Got This' Mantra
item.description:
Nvidia is currently navigating a period of significant turbulence following the sudden exit of its iconic leader Jensen Huang due to an international scandal. With the company's stock taking a hit and its market dominance facing scrutiny, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress has stepped in to steady the ship.
Over a 24-hour period, Kress publicly used the phrase "We've got this" during a third-quarter earnings call and an internal all-hands meeting. She emphasized that the company's momentum, demand, and customer partnerships remain strong, while comparing the workforce to a massive stadium crowd singing in harmony.
While some external observers question the effectiveness of the repeating mantra during a precarious position, key internal figures have embraced the message. Meanwhile, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones confirmed that the board has no intention of reinstating Huang, cementing Kress's current leadership role.

item.title: Flexell Space and ALATYR partner to study solar power for orbital data centers
item.description:
Flexell Space, a space energy company originating from Hanwha Systems, has signed a memorandum of understanding with French orbital infrastructure developer ALATYR. The partnership aims to investigate next-generation solar power solutions for space-based computing infrastructure.
ALATYR develops orbital data centers intended for artificial intelligence computing and mission-critical workloads. Its architecture features modular systems like the CITADEL infrastructure and BYLD robotics, allowing computing hardware to be replaced in orbit while retaining supporting systems. Reliable power generation is critical for these facilities, requiring solar technology to balance electrical performance, mass and launch efficiency, and long-term durability.
Flexell Space is developing next-generation space solar cells using CIGS and perovskite technologies, focusing on lightweight and flexible designs. Through this partnership, the companies will exchange technical data, assess power system compatibility, and explore potential joint development and validation opportunities for future orbital data centers.

item.title: Cloudflare Releases Updated Open-Weight Clairic and Clairic-Flash Models
item.description: According to Cloudflare AI: Background Cloudflare's Workers AI superintelligence team is developing frontier AI models targeted at customer workflows and the open-source community, focusing specifically on data extraction challenges. Architecture and Performance According to Cloudflare, the updated Clairic (a 27B model) and the new Clairic-flash (a 9-billion-parameter model) utilize a redesigned architecture featuring parallel slot autoregressive generation instead of single forward passes. This enables faster response times under one second and improved handling of unstructured text, images, and multi-page PDFs. Pricing and Availability Both models are hosted on Workers AI and released with open weights on Hugging Face. Cloudflare is offering a promotional price of $0.10 per million input tokens for both models until December 1, 2026, after which the 27B Clairic model will transition to $0.24 per million input tokens.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
item.description:
According to Google DeepMind:
Google has announced Gemini 4 Neon, a model built to deliver frontier-level intelligence with high efficiency across complex enterprise, analytical, and scientific workflows. Performance and Benchmarks According to Google's evaluations, Neon ranks #3 overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level and #2 on the Vals Index, landing on the Pareto frontier. It achieves high scores across specialized tasks, including #1 on Zapier's AutomationBench and strong results in scientific reasoning like Terminal-Bench Science. For developers, Neon supports long-running agent workflows, handles multi-file debugging, and leads the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Cost and Availability Neon is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 for cached inputs) and $15 per million output tokens, featuring a 1 million-token context window. It is rolling out via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, Google for Business, Google Antigravity, and the Gemini app for paid subscribers, with specialized cybersecurity features available through the Fairwind Program.

item.title: Vulcan rocket failure points to fuel supply issue rather than engine problem
item.description:
According to United Launch Alliance, the preliminary investigation into Sunday's failed Vulcan launch points to an inadequate supply of fuel from the vehicle to its two BE-4 engines, rather than a failure of the engines themselves. The rocket failed to reach orbit, resulting in the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites and marking ULA's first outright mission failure.
The finding clears the BE-4 engines manufactured by Blue Origin, providing some relief as the company works to return its New Glenn rocket to flight. It also clears the Centaur 5 upper stage and the solid rocket boosters, which performed normally. However, Vulcan is grounded indefinitely, leaving the U.S. Space Force and Amazon waiting for a return-to-flight date while the Federal Aviation Administration oversees the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Electrified fabric can pull fertilizer runoff out of wastewater and recycle it
item.description: How it works Researchers built the electrode by coating conductive carbon cloth with magnetite nanoparticles, which naturally bind phosphate through surface interactions. Laboratory tests showed that applying a positive voltage to this fabric more than doubles its capture efficiency compared to using no electricity. The cleanup and recycling angle Traditional methods for removing phosphate from water often involve adding chemical solutions like metal salts, which can raise costs, mess with water pH, and create secondary waste. In contrast, this electrochemical approach avoids chemical regenerants entirely during the release phase, simply requiring a reversed voltage to send the concentrated phosphate back into a solution for recovery. Next steps While the initial lab results are promising, the team notes that the technology has not yet been tested in real wastewater environments. Their upcoming plans involve scaling up the experiments and running tests using actual wastewater matrices to see how the electrified fabric holds up.

item.title: DaisyRose-27B: A New AI Model That Learns from Long Tasks to Boost Coding and Reasoning
item.description: Training Data and Setup RadixArk reports that DaisyRose-27B was trained in partnership with Eigent AI using around 1,200 curated tasks. The training process leveraged 144 H200 GPUs over 18 days, focusing on long-horizon agent tasks where each attempt could spend up to 1.5 hours in a sandbox environment with extensive tool calls. Backend Efficiency According to RadixArk, the model was trained using its internal reinforcement learning framework, Miles, in a fully asynchronous mode. The setup achieved 57% lower training cost compared to standard open-source trainers, running at about 16,800 tokens per second across the 144 GPUs. Benchmark Performance RadixArk states that DaisyRose-27B outperforms the original Qwen3.8-27B across various benchmarks, including coding, instruction following, and reasoning. The model retains a 256K-token context window and supports BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 formats.

item.title: MIT's tiny flying robot can now carry its own sensors and computers
item.description: According to MIT Robotics: Background and Payload Over the past decade, MIT researchers developed swift aerial microrobots that flap their wings like bumblebees, powered by soft artificial muscles. However, they were too light to carry the electronics needed for navigation. To solve this, the team expanded the artificial muscles by 50 percent, which increased net lift forces by 46 percent and achieved a lift-to-weight ratio of 1.9, allowing the robot to carry a 244-milligram electronics package. Sensors and Computation Without external lab cameras, the robot would normally drift off course. To fix this, researchers integrated an inertial measurement unit, an optical flow sensor, and a time-of-flight sensor, combined with a speedy sensing algorithm to calculate position and orientation rapidly. In tests, the robot successfully hovered and followed point-to-point trajectories with positional errors of only a few centimeters. Future Outlook Although the robot is still connected to an offboard power source, the electronics consume only about 6 percent of the total power. The team is now working on adding a camera for autonomous object recognition and integrating batteries to achieve completely untethered outdoor flight.

item.title: Qatar and France Sign Digital Cooperation Agreement with Focus on Quantum Tech
item.description:
According to Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, the agreement was signed in Doha on the sidelines of the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 by Qatar's Minister of Communications and Information Technology H.E. Mohammed bin Ali Al Mannai and France's Minister Delegate for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Affairs H.E. Anne Le Hénanff.
The framework establishes mechanisms for exchanging technical expertise, developing digital applications across priority economic sectors, and building local digital competencies. Minister Le Hénanff noted that both governments share a common vision of strategic autonomy in the digital sector and aligned ambitions in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies.
While the ministerial Letter of Intent is a broad information and communications technology framework without disclosed project funding or binding procurement targets, it follows closely behind growing commercial ties. Two days prior to the ministerial signing, French photonic quantum computing developer Quandela finalized a tripartite deployment alliance in Doha to bring cloud and on-premises quantum systems to the Gulf region.

item.title: Google brings the Gemini app to lower-memory Android devices
item.description:
According to Google AI:
According to Angus Logan, Builder for the Gemini App at Google, the company has re-architected the Gemini app so that its core experience can run smoothly on lower-memory Android devices. This update targets hundreds of millions of global users whose everyday internet and business connections rely on budget hardware.
With this release, eligible devices gain access to features like Gemini Live, allowing users to talk things through or practice for interviews out loud in over 45 languages. Users can also utilize their device cameras to translate documents, or create custom images. Google notes that the app can be downloaded via Google Play, accessed by holding the power button on supported phones, or found preloaded on upcoming devices from partners such as Transsion.

item.title: US Community Solar Faces Heavy Turbulence Amid Policy and Funding Changes
item.description: Over the past year, the community solar landscape in the United States has undergone significant transformation due to a wave of federal policy shifts. According to pv magazine, these challenges include the termination of the Solar for All program, the introduction of strict domestic content requirements, the removal of tax credits, and the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). The cancellation of the Solar for All initiative alone resulted in the sudden evaporation of $7 billion in critical solar development funds, dealing a severe blow to community solar projects that serve households, businesses, and non-profits. Despite these regulatory roadblocks and funding losses, consumer and business demand for clean energy remains strong, prompting individual states to bypass federal shortfalls and implement their own community-level initiatives.

item.title: CrewAI v1.15.42: Optional ChromaDB and Qdrant Defaults
item.description:
Overview of New Features
CrewAI has rolled out version 1.15.42, bringing significant adjustments to its storage architecture and agent capabilities. A major highlight is making ChromaDB an optional extra, allowing developers to leaner installations. Additionally, the framework now defaults knowledge storage to local Qdrant, decoupling storage dependencies and streamlining local vector search configurations. Bug Fixes and Enhancements
The release addresses numerous operational stability issues. It includes fixes for storing output_json values properly as JSON to prevent date formatting bugs, ensuring each Flow receives a distinct ID, and honoring max execution time limits accurately. Furthermore, it introduces security updates such as raising the soupsieve floor to version 4.0 to mitigate CVE-2026-126190, and guarantees robust UTF-8 file reading across project helpers and environment files. Installation and Usage
Developers can update or install the latest version via Python's package management tools. For projects leveraging vector databases or complex agentic workflows, reviewing the updated ChromaDB and Qdrant configurations is recommended to ensure smooth execution.

item.title: NeeevAI Founder on Bringing AI Education to Millions of Students
item.description: Expansion and Growth NeeevAI reports that its program has grown from an initial two schools in April 2025 to a projected contract base of 25,786 schools and roughly 3.1 million students by April 2027. Ecosystem and Curriculum The company's offering integrates physical and digital components, including textbooks for Classes 1 to 12, robotics kits, teacher training, and dedicated platforms like the Nova hackathon app and Argo internship app. Founder Arjun Singh Bedi emphasizes that the curriculum incorporates the UNESCO Ethical AI Framework across all grade levels to address safety, ethics, and critical thinking. Market Strategy and Partnerships NeeevAI addresses varied school infrastructure and stakeholder concerns through structured classroom integration, compliance with India's data protection rules, and practical student showcases. Bedi views major tech giants and local firms as potential partners rather than competitors, serving as a localized distribution layer between advanced technology and students.

item.title: MIT Vice President for Campus Services Joe Higgins to Step Down
item.description:
According to MIT Climate:
Joe Higgins, MIT's vice president for campus services and stewardship, will step down at the end of January and relocate to the West Coast to be closer to family, according to an announcement by Executive Vice President and Treasurer Glen Shor. Higgins joined MIT in 2016 and assumed the newly created VPCSS role in 2019, overseeing facilities, environment, health and safety, campus planning, and sustainability.
During his tenure, Higgins oversaw significant transformations, including the MIT 2030 Capital Plan projects such as the Schwarzman College of Computing and preparations for the MIT Quantum Initiative. He also contributed to reducing MIT's overall campus Facilities Condition Index by about 40 percent and advanced campus climate goals, helping the Institute approach net-zero carbon emissions through energy-efficiency projects and large-scale renewable energy partnerships.
Following his departure, Jon Alvarez will serve as interim VPCSS while executive search firm Isaacson, Miller leads a national search for a permanent successor.

item.title: BMS Alzheimer’s drug shows promise but safety questions remain
item.description:
Bristol Myers Squibb presented early data from its Phase 3 ADEPT program at the CTAD conference, testing the drug KarXT (marketed as Cobenfy) for psychosis associated with Alzheimer’s disease. Data from two studies, ADEPT-1 and ADEPT-3, showed improvements in symptoms like hallucinations and delusions.
However, treatment-emergent adverse events affected over half of the patients, reaching 56.6% in one study and 65% in the other, raising tolerability concerns. Analysts from Truist Securities noted that the current data lacks a placebo control and does not address the main trial endpoint of relapse prevention. The definitive randomized results are expected in 2027.
